title: Permutation Coloring Game
statementMd:
Alice and Bob are playing a game. They have a permutation 𝑝p of length 𝑛n — an array of 𝑛n elements in which every integer from 11 to 𝑛n occurs exactly once. Initially, every element of the permutation is colored white.

The players take turns; Alice goes first. On each turn, the current player chooses between 11 and 𝑘k white elements and colors all of them either red or blue. All elements chosen on the same turn must receive the same color.

The game ends when there are no white elements left. If the resulting permutation can be sorted in increasing order by swapping elements of the same color, Alice wins. Otherwise, Bob wins. Any two elements may be swapped as long as they have the same color.

Determine who wins if both players play optimally.

## Input

The first line contains one integer 𝑡t (1≤𝑡≤1041≤t≤104) — the number of test cases.

Each test case consists of two lines:

- the first line contains two integers 𝑛n and 𝑘k (2≤𝑛≤2⋅1052≤n≤2⋅105; 1≤𝑘≤min(20,𝑛)1≤k≤min(20,n)) — the length of the permutation and the maximum number of elements that can be colored in one turn;
- the second line contains 𝑛n pairwise distinct integers 𝑝1,𝑝2,…,𝑝𝑛p1,p2,…,pn (1≤𝑝𝑖≤𝑛1≤pi≤n).

Additional constraints on the input:

- the sum of 𝑛n over all test cases does not exceed 2⋅1052⋅105.

## Output

For each test case, print `Alice` on a separate line if Alice wins, or `Bob` if Bob wins.
